subject: Demo recap: priorities, decision criteria, and interop test plan
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sanders <emily.sanders@cloudpointhealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Demo recap: priorities, decision criteria, and interop test plan

Emily — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick written recap so we’re aligned and nothing falls through the cracks. Notes below pulled from our call + proposed next tests.

Top pain points you called out:
- Latency variability impacting clinician UX (need p95 under 150ms for short queries, p95 under 500ms for multi-turn summaries).
- Embedding cost and search latency when scaling to ~2M patient vectors.
- Data isolation & auditability for PHI (VPC, retention controls, KMS).
- Predictable throughput during peak clinic hours (concurrent requests spike 500–1,000/s).

Stated goals / decision criteria (what will move the deal):
1) Performance SLOs: p95 latency targets + clear degradation behavior.
2) Cost per med-note request (target: < $0.01/request at expected QPS).
3) Security & compliance evidence (SOC 2, KMS integrations, audit logs).
4) Smooth integration with your vector store + ability to run a private deployment later.

Proposed follow-up tests (agreeing these will inform a POC scope):
A) Throughput & latency run: 30-minute steady-state at 800 concurrent users, report p50/p95/p99 and tail-burst behavior. (Owner: Marcus)
B) Embedding cost/latency comparison: 100k vectors ingest + 10k queries, measure indexing time and search latency with and without quantization. (Owner: Marcus)
C) Security baseline: provide SOC2 summary and run a short audit checklist for data-in-flight/in-rest controls; confirm KMS flow for your keys. (Owner: Priya)
D) Failover flows: simulate region outage and validate model fallback behavior and routing policy. (Owner: Jordan)

Attachments I’m sharing now: demo recording, a first-draft MOP (mutual action plan), and a starter interop test matrix. Please treat the MOP as draft — we’ll iterate on dates and owners.

Next steps / asks for CloudPoint:
- Emily: confirm the procurement timeline (you mentioned an internal review next week) and whether Rachel from procurement should be looped on contract conversations.
- Emily: can you confirm a sample dataset (sanitized) we can use for the embedding cost/latency test?
- We’ll propose exact test windows and calendar invites by EOD Wednesday PST.

If that all looks right I’ll lock owners and send calendar invites for the throughput run and a short security sync.

—
Priya Natarajan
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

- Procurement: Rachel will run a 2-week review starting next Tues 11/10; we’re hoping to have budget sign-off by end of November. I’ve CC’d Rachel.

Couple of questions:
1) For the throughput run, will you need access to our staging auth (SAML) or can we run against a tokenized test app?
2) Can you provide an estimated pricing band for the POC (monthly) so Procurement has a number to evaluate?

Looking forward to the next steps.

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Demo recap: priorities, decision criteria, and interop test plan

Looping in some technical detail to drive the test plan — notes for the team and for Emily if helpful.

Throughput & latency run (A):
- Test scaffolding: k6 + our request generator against the same model config as demo (Llama-2-13B q4f16 / prod variant).
- Scenarios: 1) Short clinical question (avg tokens 40), 2) Multi-turn summary (avg tokens 600).
- Targets to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, CPU/GPU utilization, kv-cache hit rate, and memory pressure.
- Duration & sizing: 30m steady state + 5x 1m spike tests at 1,200 QPS.
- Data required: sample prompt patterns + a token budget estimate.

Embedding cost test (B):
- Run both dense and OPQ-quantized embeddings for 100k vectors on our dedicated config; measure ingest time, index size, query latency at 50 qps.
- Deliverable: CSV with throughput, average latency, and cost estimate at your projected scale (2M vectors).

Security baseline (C) & KMS:
- We’ll share SOC2 summary and a short KMS diagram. For a POC we normally accept a tokenized staging flow; if you need SAML we’ll timebox the engineering work (2–4 days).

Attachments I added: interop-test-matrix.csv (detailed scenarios + metrics) and a quick pricing band export for a 30-day POC (pricing-band.xlsx).

I’ll sketch the test job configs and ping Emily with proposed windows Thursday.

—
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
